conclusion: Primary sustained 30 fps limit is an explicit ArkUI/app frame-rate vote and 33.33 ms VSync delivery. The body still has occasional work exceeding a 16.67 ms budget. Completion separately destroys the streaming List item, rebuilds the history item, and resets List item geometry, producing a large catch-up scroll.

ChatPage.ets chatTimelineActiveTail uses a separate ForEach(this.streamingTail) with tail-messageId keys.
applyConversationRunSnapshot assigns completed rows and empties streamingTail, so item identity cannot persist between these ForEach parents.
MarkdownText.updateDisplay returns early when content equals lastParsedText; onStreamingChanged alone does not trigger this reconstruction.
The old reasoning Scroll already ended at 3.014 s. Final new reasoning is collapsed by default when autoCloseThinking is enabled. This is not a 5900-unit reasoning height expansion.

No additional list item index appears during the jump window: history grows 1 to 2 and tail shrinks 1 to 0. Action footer is rebuilt within the same new row. A suggestions tail cannot explain the observed item-top reset from -5649.64 to +294.

limitations: No sched trace category was captured, so OnVsync durations are elapsed slice times, not isolated CPU execution times.
App FrameCallback is not individually marked. ArkUI delivered VSync/DispatchDisplaySync frequency and scrollBy calls are observable, but callback internals cannot be directly attributed.
Trace labels UI_ANIMATION but does not identify which exact component produced the generic 30 fps vote. Native scroll explicitly produced scrollable_multi_task_scene preferred rate 120.
Trace captures geometry and reconstruction, not pixels. Visual flash and exact perceived jump require screen recording/screenshot confirmation.
Engine scroll offsets are retained as raw trace values; no unsupported physical-pixel/vp conversion was applied.
